## In this session

-   Space and place in humanities data
-   **Hands-on** with the [DARIAH Geo-Browser](https://geobrowser.de.dariah.eu/) and
    [Palladio](https://hdlab.stanford.edu/palladio/)

## Mapping humanities data

-   The gap between a **place** and a **coordinate**, and everything that falls into it
-   Geocoding and gazetteers: [GeoNames](https://www.geonames.org/),
    [Wikidata](https://www.wikidata.org/), [Pleiades](https://pleiades.stoa.org/)
-   Historical geography: borders move, names change, places disappear
-   The base map is an argument. A modern map under early modern data is a claim.
-   Time plus space: how to show change without implying a smooth process

## Hands-on

Working from your Wikidata CSV ([Session 5](/contents/sessions/05.qmd)) or from any other
place-bearing dataset:

1.  **DARIAH Geo-Browser** — georeferencing a table, and animating it over time
2.  **Palladio** — map, graph, gallery and table views over the same data; the point is the
    switching between them
3.  Deliberately break something: map an ambiguous place name and see where it lands

### Reflection

-   Which of your points are wrong, and how would a reader ever know?
-   What does the visualisation make it *impossible* to say?

::: {.callout-tip title="In parallel in the Lab"}
The [DH Lab](https://dhbern.github.io/dh-lab/contents/sessions/10.html) does data cleaning and
reconciliation with OpenRefine — the tool that fixes exactly the place-name problems this
session exposes.
:::
